A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DORA research, with readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Retained experiments and relocated material can be reliably matched despite the additional experiments in v2.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original accuracy, pass-rate, computational-cost and latency results on mathematical reasoning benchmarks, including a difficulty-stratified analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and adds benchmark results, intermediate-success measurements, clustering ablations and robustness experiments in Section 4 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: DORA's embedding similarities, softmax-diagonal uniqueness weights, reward reweighting and rollout allocation remain unchanged in Equations 10–13, as does Algorithm 1. The new hard-clustering ablations evaluate alternatives without replacing the proposed soft-clustering procedure.

E1.justification: v2 retains MATH500, AIME2024 and AIME2025 and adds actual evaluations on HMMT24, HMMT25, AMC23 and AMC24 in Table 1. These broaden the represented competition problems, question formats and difficulty distributions substantially within mathematical reasoning.

E2.justification: Temperature Sampling, Beam Search, DVTS and REBASE remain the search baselines. Table 4 newly evaluates KMeans and hierarchical-clustering alternatives against DORA's soft clustering, providing a limited extension of the evaluated comparison methods.

E3.justification: New configurations include LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct with Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-72B, Skywork-PRM-7B, alternative embeddings and parameter sweeps. Table 3 introduces a diagnostic that stops search after K steps and completes trajectories through temperature sampling. These substantially extend the evaluation design; the original main rollout budgets and decoding defaults remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds intermediate search-guidance analysis, hard-versus-soft clustering ablations, model-scale and PRM-family robustness tests, and temperature and embedding sensitivity studies in Tables 3–8. The existing difficulty analysis is retained in Appendix D.1 and Figure 5, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: The efficiency comparison changes from point estimates in v1 Table 1 to explicit mean-and-standard-deviation reporting over three runs in v2 Table 2. Existing plot bands and the general five-run MATH500 and ten-run AIME statements remain. The three-run caption is not reconciled with those general statements; an increase in runs is not established.

E6.justification: The original performance plots, difficulty curves and MATH500 efficiency means are retained, but substantial results are added. For example, Table 5 reports 80.6 accuracy for DORA versus 79.2 for REBASE with the larger policy–PRM pair. Table 4 reports 68.7 for soft clustering versus 68.0 for the best KMeans setting. Added AIME24 efficiency results show equal 14.7 accuracy for DORA at 64 rollouts and REBASE at 256 rollouts.

T1.justification: The Bayesian formulation, Assumption 1, Propositions 1–2, Theorem 1 and their Appendix B proofs are unchanged. Appendix C retains the same Beta-distribution explanation. The new empirical diagnostics introduce no revised formal theory or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about optimal resource allocation, solution-level redundancy bias, DORA's optimality and improved efficiency. The conclusion still reports the same 3.5-fold FLOPs reduction and fourfold latency reduction. Additional experiments support these retained contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 adds an interpretation of semantic grouping as improving intermediate search guidance. Appendix D adds explanations for hard-clustering weaknesses, degraded reward guidance at high temperature, embedding-capacity effects and robustness across model and PRM families. These substantially expand the mechanism and applicability discussion; the original limitations concerning PRM availability and low-confidence assumptions remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-and-data release announcement with a repository pointer, plus technical information for the added experiments, including embedding-model sizes and tested parameter ranges. The original decoding settings, hardware description and prompt are retained in Implementation Details, moved from Appendix D to Appendix E.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds brief positioning against branch-and-prune and dynamic-decomposition approaches, citing TreeBoN, DISC, early-stopping self-consistency and difficulty-adaptive self-consistency. Appendix D also introduces the MTEB citation. The central novelty claim and existing related-work organization remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose, including the abstract, introduction, theory and conclusion, is retained. Changes include localized experimental explanations, moving the difficulty discussion into a new More Experiments appendix, renumbering Implementation Details, and adding acknowledgements and a NeurIPS checklist. These do not amount to extensive rewriting of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds dedicated benchmark, intermediate-step and ablation tables, substantially expanding the results presentation. The original efficiency table becomes a dataset-grouped table with standard deviations. The difficulty plot moves from the main text to the appendix as Figure 5, while the Beta-prior plot becomes Figure 4; their plotted content is retained.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked direct tests of its clustering choice and dependence on temperatures, embeddings and PRM configurations. Tables 3–8 substantially address those empirical gaps through mechanism diagnostics and controlled robustness comparisons, strengthening support for DORA's central design. Broader benchmark coverage and explicit efficiency-result standard deviations further improve assessment. The unresolved three-run versus five/ten-run reporting discrepancy is a limitation, but the added validation provides a substantial net quality gain.
